subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: Capturing fleeting light and everyday scenes with loose brushwork
questions.explain: Impressionists used loose, visible brushstrokes to capture changing light and ordinary moments.

questions.q: Salvador Dali is associated with which art movement?
questions.explain: Salvador Dali was a leading Surrealist, known for dream-like works such as his melting clocks.

options: The appearance of texture created on a flat surface
Texture you can physically feel on the surface
questions.explain: Visual texture is the illusion of texture on a flat surface, whereas actual texture can be touched.

questions.q: How are complementary colours defined on the colour wheel?
options: Colours that sit next to each other
Different tones of the same hue
Colours that sit directly opposite each other
questions.explain: Complementary colours are positioned opposite one another on the colour wheel, such as red and green.

questions.q: In GCSE Art, the assessment objective about 'recording' asks you to...
options: Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to your intentions
Write an essay with no images
questions.explain: The recording objective is about capturing observations and ideas, for example through drawing and photography.

questions.q: A 'hue' refers to which property of colour?
options: The pure colour itself, such as red or blue
questions.explain: Hue is the name of the pure colour, such as red, yellow or blue, before tints or shades are added.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'annotation' in a sketchbook?
options: To explain your thinking, choices and development in words
To list the cost of materials
To fill empty space with decoration
questions.explain: Annotation uses written notes to explain your ideas, decisions and how your work is developing.
Abstract Expressionism used large-scale, energetic, often non-figurative gestural marks.

questions.q: What is the key difference between shape and form?
options: Shape is two-dimensional, form is three-dimensional
Shape is coloured, form is not
Shape is large, form is small
questions.explain: A shape is flat and two-dimensional, while a form has depth and appears three-dimensional.

questions.q: In a composition, what is the 'focal point'?
options: The main area that draws the viewer's eye
The darkest area of the picture
questions.explain: The focal point is the part of the composition that attracts the viewer's attention first.

questions.q: What does 'tone' refer to in the formal elements?
options: The lightness or darkness of an area
questions.explain: Tone describes how light or dark an area is, helping to create the illusion of form.

options: The arrangement of elements within an artwork
The size of the canvas only
questions.explain: Composition is how the visual elements are arranged and organised within the picture area.
